questions.evidence:
The review group prepares five cards: renewal, steady, detour, hidden, and handover. Their task is to explain the words through short actions. A reader must be able to understand the situation without seeing the lesson from which the word originally came.

A student waiting for a later library due date is checking a renewal. Someone keeping a page from moving holds it steady. A walker using an alternate path around roadwork follows a detour. The group keeps each explanation focused on the action that matters.

For hidden, they describe a bag detail that has not been made public. Handover belongs beside the moment a checked item is returned to its owner. One student says the act of finding a bag is already a handover, but a partner points out that no receiver is involved yet.

The students add a receiver to the sentence and read it again. They finish by asking what extra detail makes each word fit. This small habit helps them avoid choosing an answer merely because it belongs to the general topic of the passage.

Handover—giving a checked item to its owner.
